posts.trend: Indian Woman Pays Rs 10 Lakh Monthly Rent For 2-Bedroom Apartment In New York City, Sparks Debate
posts.context: Urban Indian tenants face extreme local housing demands and compare themselves to international rent outrages.
posts.angle: A rental broker in Mumbai or Bangalore sees international luxury rents not as news, but as a challenge.
slides: A broker in Indiranagar has seen the ₹10 lakh NYC apartment and got inspired.

No sunlight.
Seepage on the bedroom wall.
Ten months of deposit upfront.
No bachelors.
No non-veg.

But they want a LinkedIn profile of your pet.

The appraisal is final.
posts.caption: Send this to the person who spent their weekend arguing with a broker on WhatsApp. 🔑
posts.rank_verdict: The landing's sudden pivot to corporate appraisal terminology in a housing joke is highly confusing and breaks the premise.
